title: Why zero can break a plan
idea: Dividing by zero is impossible - the program errors. Spotting a possible zero divisor is the first edge-case skill. Thinking, no code.

exercises.prompt: What happens if a program tries to compute 10 / 0?
options: It errors - dividing by zero is not allowed
exercises.explanation: Division by zero is undefined, so Python raises an error and stops. You must avoid it.

exercises.prompt: You can safely divide any number by zero and get zero.
exercises.explanation: No. Dividing by zero is impossible and causes an error - it does not quietly give zero.

exercises.prompt: 'total / count gives the average.' When is this dangerous?
exercises.explanation: If count is zero, total / count divides by zero and crashes. The zero count is the edge case.

exercises.prompt: In 'price / people', which variable must NOT be zero?
exercises.explanation: The divisor (people) must not be zero. A zero price is fine - zero people is the problem.

exercises.prompt: Match each division to the value that must not be zero.
exercises.explanation: In each case the bottom number (the divisor) must not be zero, or the division errors.

exercises.prompt: 'miles / gallons gives miles-per-gallon.' The edge case is...
exercises.explanation: Zero gallons means dividing by zero. A zero miles value is fine; zero gallons is the danger.

exercises.prompt: Before dividing, it is wise to ask whether the divisor could ever be zero.
exercises.explanation: Exactly. Checking the divisor for zero first is how you guard against the crash.

exercises.prompt: Which of these divisions is always safe (the divisor can never be zero)?
exercises.explanation: total / 2 has a fixed divisor of 2, which is never zero. The others divide by a variable that might be zero.

exercises.prompt: A zero divisor is an edge case because...
options: it is a rare value that breaks the normal division
it is the most common value
exercises.explanation: Most of the time the divisor is fine; the rare zero is what breaks the plan. That is what makes it an edge case.

exercises.prompt: The safe habit before any division is...
options: Check the divisor is not zero first
exercises.explanation: Guard the divisor: only divide when it is not zero. The next lessons show how a simple if does this.
